title: Protocol for Isolation and Characterization of In Situ Fixed Quiescent Muscle Stem Cells
protocol: Place a 250 mL beaker with cold 1× PBS on ice, 30 mL per mouse.
Label the beaker containing 1× PBS as “PBS.”
Prepare 0.5% PFA solution freshly, 30 mL per mouse.
Place a 250 mL beaker with cold 0.5% PFA on ice.
Label the beaker containing 0.5% PFA as “PFA.”
Place a 250 mL beaker with cold 2 M glycine on ice, 30 mL per mouse.
Label the beaker containing 2 M glycine as “Glycine.”
Prepare the perfusion syringe by adapting a 25-gauge needle to a 10 mL syringe.
Label three syringes as “PBS,” “PFA,” and “Glycine,” respectively.
Anesthetize the mouse with ∼400 μL of 1.2% Avertin solution through intraperitoneal injection.
Stabilize the mouse's feet using tapes/needles after anesthesia.
Open the chest and expose the heart for perfusion.
Use forceps to pick up the skin around the bottom of the sternum.
Make an incision using a pair of scissors.
Lift the bottom of the sternum with the forceps.
Cut along the diaphragm using the scissors.
Hold the forceps high and keep the scissor tip up to avoid damaging organs.
Lift the rib cage and expose the heart.
Make an incision on the right atrium using the scissors.
Use blunt-end forceps to gently hold the heart.
Pierce the heart near the bottom of the left ventricle using the perfusion syringe.
Perfuse 10 mL cold PBS using a 10 mL syringe with a 25G needle to wash away blood.
Stabilize the syringe with blunt-end forceps during perfusion, ensuring the tip remains slightly tilted upwards at approximately 60° above horizontal.
Maintain the needle's position in the left ventricle throughout perfusion.
Perfuse an additional 10 mL cold PBS twice, for a total of 30 mL PBS.
Mix 10 mL of cold 0.5% PFA in a 10 mL syringe with a 25-gauge needle.
Perfuse the mixture through the tissue three times, totaling 30 mL.
Perform each perfusion at a rate of approximately 10 mL per minute by hand.
Start a 5 min timer immediately after beginning the perfusions.
Wait for the timer to ring to ensure a total fixation time of 5 minutes.
Perfuse 10 mL cold 2 M glycine using a 10 mL syringe with a 25-gauge needle.
Repeat perfusion twice more, for a total of three times.
Pour approximately 10 mL of cold wash medium into a 10 cm glass petri dish.
Dissect the hindlimb muscles out using a No. 11 blade and scissors.
Place dissected muscle pieces in the petri dish containing wash medium.
Remove muscle pieces from the dish.
Mince the muscle pieces with a No. 20 blade on the cover of the glass petri dish.
Pour approximately 2 mL of the first enzyme digestion solution to the minced muscle slurry.
Cut the mixture further using scissors.
Return the muscle slurry back into the first enzyme digestion solution in a 50 mL conical tube.
Wrap the cap of the 50 mL tube with parafilm to prevent leakage.
Place the tube in a 37°C shaking water bath at medium-high speed for 90 minutes.
Pre-cool the centrifuge 5408R to 4°C (optional).
After enzyme digestion, fill the tube with cold Wash Medium to total 50 mL and mix by flipping upside down several times.
Pour half of the slurry (25 ml) into another tube.
Fill both tubes with cold Wash Medium to reach a total volume of 50 mL each.
Centrifuge at 500 × g, 4°C for 10 minutes using centrifuge 5408R.
Warm Collagenase II and Dispase II aliquots on a 37°C heat block during centrifugation.
Take the tubes out carefully after centrifugation.
Aspirate away Wash Medium until approximately 12.5 mL solution remains.
Place a 1 mL pipette tip in front of the aspirator to avoid aspirating too fast and disrupting the pellet.
Add 1 mL Collagenase II (3,000 U/mL) and 1 mL Dispase II (30 U/mL) to a tube.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times using a 25 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the solution with enzymes to another tube.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5 times using the same 25 mL serological pipette.
Add cold Wash Medium to bring the total volume to 30 mL.
Put the tube into a 37°C shaking water bath at medium-high speed for 30 min.
After the second enzyme digestion, mix the cell solution using a 30 mL syringe adapted to a 20-gauge needle ten times.
Filter the cell solution with a 40 μm filter adapted to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Add cold Wash Medium to bring the total volume to 50 mL.
Centrifuge at 500 × g, 4°C, for 10 min using centrifuge 5408R.
Take the tubes out carefully.
Use the aspirator to aspirate away the Wash Medium until ∼2–3 mL solution remains.
Place a 1 mL pipette tip in front of the aspirator to avoid aspirating too fast.
Place a 200 μL pipette tip in front of the aspirator when the solution goes down to ∼15 mL, and do not disrupt the pellet.
Aspirate until the solution reaches 2–3 mL.
Use a 1 mL pipette to resuspend the cell solution.
Filter the cell solution with a 40 μm filter adapted to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer the single-cell suspension to a 5 mL round-bottom polypropylene tube as the loading tube.
If using size calibration beads for size reference, dilute individual size beads at around 1:100 in PBS respectively in each loading tube (i.e., add 3 μL beads to 297 μL PBS).
Sonicate the beads before usage to avoid aggregates.
Load individual size beads and record ∼1,000–2,000 events for each bead.
Sort cells using a cell sorter.
For Pax7nGFP mice, SCs are marked by GFP signals.
Gate for singlets and then the GFP+ population.
Collect the sorted cells in a 5 mL round-bottom polypropylene tube with 1 mL cold Wash Medium.
Centrifuge the cell at 15,000 × g, 4°C for 3 min using a pre-chilled centrifuge.
Pipette away the supernatant.
Snap freeze the cell pellet using liquid N2.
Store the cell pellet at −80°C.
Add 100 μL buffer PKD to the sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 10 μL proteinase K to the mixture.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate at 56°C for 1 h.
Cool down the tubes on ice.
Centrifuge at 20,000 × g, 20°C–25°C (room temperature in lab, RT) for 20 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 10 μL DNase Booster Buffer and 10 μL DNase I stock solution to the sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate at RT for 15 min.
Add 320 μL buffer RBC to the mixture.
Mix well by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Transfer 700 μL sample to the RNeasy MinElute spin column.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g, 30 s at RT.
Discard the flow-through.
Repeat transferring and centrifuging until all sample has passed through the column.
Add 500 μL buffer RPE to the column.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g, 30 s at RT.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 500 μL buffer RPE to the column.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g, 30 s at RT.
Discard the flow-through.
Place the column into a new 2 mL collection tube, open the lid of the spin column, and centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 5 min.
Place the column into a new 1.5 mL collection tube.
Add 14 μL RNase-free water to the membrane of the column.
Wait for 5 min.
Close the lip during elution.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 1 min.
Discard the column.
Keep the collection tube.
Take 1 μL RNA for quantification using Qubit RNA HS Assay.
Store the RNA at -80°C.
Use alternative RNA quantification method if suitable for low input.
The isolated RNA is now compatible for traditional cDNA generation methods such as the SMART-seq 2 protocol.
